headline: High-risk shared-workspace pair: Windsurf can read/write local files and use MCP while Airbyte has broad network egress, creating dangerous leakage and cascading-action pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Windsurf can read workspace files, use MCP, and process clipboard content; Airbyte can emit API-driven outputs and has broad network egress. A shared local workspace or copied content creates a plausible instruction-hijack path, though no direct parser bridge is documented. Uncertainty about the exact orchestration pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Airbyte outputs are copied into Windsurf via clipboard or workspace files
IF Windsurf treats file or MCP content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents
Keep Airbyte outputs in a read-only export folder
Require explicit provenance tags before Windsurf follows file content
Use separate workspaces for each agent
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or instruction-stripping before transfer

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; Windsurf reads workspace files, uses MCP, and can write files. If they share a filesystem, Windsurf can expose sensitive business data through its model proxy or MCP paths. The pair’s default local-file sharing makes leakage materially plausible.
conditions: IF Airbyte writes business data into a workspace visible to Windsurf
IF Windsurf sends that content through its model proxy or an MCP server
mitigations: Separate Airbyte and Windsurf workspaces
Restrict Windsurf to non-sensitive directories
Disable MCP servers for sensitive projects
Use redacted sample data only
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on file reads and outbound prompts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and shared_state_with_other_instances via local filesystem; Airbyte can also interact with APIs and broad network egress. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide. The shared-state mechanism makes this a default-dangerous conflict.
conditions: IF both agents target the same local repository or workspace
IF Windsurf auto-executes commands while Airbyte writes generated artifacts
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Turn off auto-execute in Windsurf
Use git locks or a single committer workflow
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutual exclusion

D_cascading_error.rationale: Windsurf can act on files and git state, so if it consumes Airbyte-produced artifacts as authoritative, errors can cascade into code or config changes. Airbyte’s outputs are not inherently verified by Windsurf, but the pair does not prove an automatic action chain in all setups, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Airbyte-generated files are treated as ground truth by Windsurf
IF Windsurf is allowed to commit or edit based on those files without review
mitigations: Require human review before commits
Mark Airbyte outputs as untrusted inputs
Add checksum or schema validation before use
Disable auto-commit workflows
requires-engineering: add verification gates between generation and action

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte handles business data, while Windsurf handles source code, open files, and model-provider keys. If business data or regulated content is placed into Windsurf’s workspace, retention and third-party processing policies may diverge. The profiles do not show a specific residency mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated business data is copied into Windsurf-managed files
IF Windsurf forwards that content to a third-party model proxy or MCP server
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Windsurf workspaces
Use synthetic or masked datasets
Review vendor retention settings before use
Separate secrets from code workspaces
requires-engineering: document and enforce data-handling boundaries
